groups.root_cause: On Darwin, processes are treated as owned by the invocation if they share its working directory and started after it, so unrelated processes get killed.

Descendant discovery depends on inherited environment markers and working-directory heuristics, so helpers with a replaced environment are missed even when they share the process group. Shutdown is then reported as complete while they are still alive.
The rerun path after a gate timeout calls cleanup without the retry/recovery handling used elsewhere, so one cleanup failure ends the run.
